name: Constrain automatic IDE task execution from untrusted repositories

attribution.legal_posture: First-party provider adversary emulation and defensive guidance describe a DPRK-linked fake-interview malware path; candidate hiring and DPRK IT-worker status require separate evidence.

caveats: Name similarity, profile images, avatars, code style, language, geography, account age, follower graphs, stars, forks, contribution volume and repository topic require corroboration before supporting legal identity, nationality, common operator or DPRK affiliation.

Keep applicant messages, resumes, emails, phone numbers, identity documents, biometrics, private repositories, credentials, tokens, payment data, wallets, raw device or network selectors, active infrastructure and copied malware code out of the record.
Accounts described by these sources remain unpublished, uncontacted, unfollowed, unstarred, unforked, unmessaged, and unprobed.
Fake-interview malware remains analytically separate from fraudulent employment unless an exact source explicitly establishes overlap.
Keep DPRK-linked fake-interview malware analytically separate from fraudulent employment unless an exact source establishes overlap.
Keep this abstract GitLab defensive control publishable as a control; candidate attribution requires separate evidence.
This record covers defense against a DPRK-linked fake-interview malware path; candidate assessment requires separate evidence. Executable code and live indicators stay unpublished.
The record scope excludes person, persona, account, organization, repository, domain, contact value, executable code, active infrastructure selector, and applicant artifact.

Treat researcher and vendor attributions as claims with source, date, confidence, and limitation. Persona and account labels carry source-level identity status; civil identity is outside those labels.
Use multiple independently explainable signals, trained human review, documented reasons, proportional collection, bounded retention, and a correction or appeal path.
Verify exact package status and technical behavior independently before operational blocking; package-name similarity can create false positives.

infrastructure.statement: GitLab describes fake-interview repositories using IDE task configuration to launch background subprocesses after a developer grants workspace trust. GitLab's team emulated the path, distinguished background task-spawn behavior from user-initiated terminal activity, and combined runtime detection with fleet hardening and developer education.
defensive_use: Treat repositories supplied during recruiting, take-home work, code review, or unsolicited collaboration as untrusted input.
Disable or centrally constrain automatic IDE task execution where practical, and make workspace-trust decisions explicit.
Use endpoint telemetry to distinguish hidden background task subprocesses from user-initiated foreground development activity, then tune for the organization's normal environment.
Open and test candidate code only in isolated, disposable environments without production credentials, secrets, wallets, or unrestricted network access.
infrastructure.evidence_class: first-party provider adversary emulation and endpoint control
